findings.title: Exhausted federated recovery codes removed with wrong API
findings.body: In RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.isRecoveryAuthnCodeInputValid the code loads the credential with RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential() which can return a federated (user-storage) credential, then calls authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(id) when allCodesUsed(). removeStoredCredentialById() only removes local Keycloak-DB credentials, not federated credentials which require disableCredentialType/remove federated handling. Consequence: when recovery codes live in user storage and are exhausted they are never deleted/disabled, isConfiguredFor stays true and used codes may remain accepted, plus the required-action re-add logic operates on stale state.

findings.title: Federated recovery credential drops label and timestamp
findings.body: CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential() builds UserCredentialModel("", credentialModel.getType(), recoveryCodesJson) where recoveryCodesJson is only the JSON array of raw codes. The userLabel and generatedAt contained in the passed RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel are never transferred to the user-storage provider. Consequence: a recovery credential stored in user storage permanently loses its label/metadata, unlike the local-DB path which persists them via credentialModel, and any UI/account display or audit depending on them shows null/wrong values.

findings.title: getCredentials discards stored recovery credential ID
findings.body: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials() reconstructs the recovery credential with RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(...) but never copies the ID assigned in updateCredential() (via KeycloakModelUtils.generateId()). It returns a model with a fresh/transient ID. Consequence: RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential() returns an ID that does not match the stored federated credential, so removeStoredCredentialById(), account-console delete, and any lookup by ID operate on a non-existent ID and silently fail, leaving the real credential orphaned.

findings.title: Federated recovery codes cannot be disabled/removed
findings.body: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.disableCredentialType() only handles OTP types and getDisableableCredentialTypesStream() only advertises OTP, while supportsCredentialType/isConfiguredFor/updateCredential/isValid all handle RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE. Consequence: admin disableCredentialType, account-console credential delete, and exhausted-code cleanup can never remove a federated recovery credential, so tests asserting no DB credentials pass while the federated credential is effectively undeletable.

findings.title: Federated recovery code validation does not consume codes
findings.body: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid() for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE only checks generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse())) and never removes/marks the used code. The local Keycloak recovery-code provider consumes a code on successful validation so it is single-use. Consequence: federated recovery codes can be replayed indefinitely, and the new testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin test logging in once cannot detect reuse or allCodesUsed cleanup failures.
